25. INTERPRETATION AND CONCLUSIONS  
This Report summarises the results of an updated Feasibility Study for the Nyanzaga Gold Project, which 
demonstrates the technical and economic viability of a large open pit mining operation  and gravity/CIL 
process flowsheet on the Nyanzaga and Kilimani orebodies. Risks and uncertainties that could reasonably be 
expected to affect the reliability or confidence in the exploration information, Mineral Resource or Mineral 
Reserve estimates, or projected economic outcomes are discussed below. 
25.1 MINERAL RESOURCES 
Data that inform the Mineral Resource estimate are considered to be representative and free of any biases 
or other factors that may materially impact the reliability of the sampling or significantly affect confidence in 
estimated resources. Checks to confirm the validity of the drilling database indicate that it forms a sufficiently 
reliable basis for resource estimation. 
Drilling activities are ongoing at the Nyanzaga Gold Project with a focus on infill and depth extensions at the 
Nyanzaga and Kilimani deposits, as well as early-stage exploration on granted tenure. 
The Nyanzaga Gold Project Mineral Resource estimates could be affected by: 
• Future, yet unknown environmental, permitting, legal, title, taxation, socio -economic, marketing, 
political, or other relevant issues. 
• Metal price assumptions. 
• Changes to the technical inputs used to estimate gold content (e.g., bulk densities, grade estimation 
strategies, and interpolation methodologies). 
• Changes to the geological interpretation (e.g., intrusive dykes and structural offsets such as faults and 
shear zones) and mineralisation (domain) geometry and continuity of mineralised zones and grade. 
• Depletion due to previous mining activities. 
• Changes to geotechnical and mining assumptions, including the minimum mining thickness; or the 
application of alternative mining methods. 
• Changes to process plant recovery estimates. 
• Changes to the assumptions used to calculate the gold cut-off grades. 
25.2 MINERAL RESERVES 
Perseus has performed an economic analysis related to the Nyanzaga Gold Project to a Feasibility Study level 
of accuracy at the forecasted metal prices, production rates, metal recoveries, and capital and operating 
costs estimated in this Report. Perseus confirms that the positive economic outcome supports the Mineral 
Reserve estimate. 
The QP is of the opinion that Mineral Reserves were estimated using industry -accepted practices and 
conform to the CIM Definition Standards and the JORC Code. Mineral Reserves stated in this report are based 
on open pit mining methods. The Mineral Reserves are acceptable to support mine planning. 
As noted in Section 15.5, the reported Mineral Reserve may be affected by future study assessments of 
mining, processing, environmental, permitting, taxation, socio-economic and other factors. 
Additional technical factors which may affect the Mineral Reserve estimate include: 
• Metal price assumptions. 
• Changes to the technical inputs used to estimate gold content (e.g., bulk densities, grade estimation 
strategies, and interpolation methodologies).

• Changes to the geological interpretation (e.g., intrusive dykes and structural offsets such as faults and 
shear zones) and mineralisation (domain) geometry and continuity of mineralised zones and grade 
assumptions. 
• Changes to geotechnical and mining assumptions, including the minimum mining thickness; or the 
application of alternative mining methods. 
• Changes to process plant recovery estimates. 
• Changes to the assumptions used to calculate the gold cut-off grades. 
25.3 MINING METHODS 
Open pit mining of the Nyanzaga Gold Project is considered reasonable and technically viable based on the 
parameters and assumptions contained within this report, and based on Perseus’ extensive open pit mining 
experience in other African jurisdictions. Estimates of open pit Mineral Reserves, mining parameters, costs 
and revenues are well understood and can be considered reliable predictors of the future mining 
performance at Nyanzaga. 
25.4 MINERAL PROCESSING AND METALLURGICAL TESTING 
The results of comminution and metallurgical test work conducted across the Nyanzaga and Kilimani deposits 
are considered by the QP to be of sufficient scope and quality to support the proposed process plant design 
and production planning. 
Comminution testing determined that oxide ores are between very low competency to competent, are 
between very soft and hard, and are between non-abrasive and abrasive; and fresh ores are between low 
competency to very competent, are medium hard to very hard, and are between slightly abrasive and 
abrasive. The single stage crushing and SAB comminution circuit selected can accommodate the spectrum of 
material hardness and competency observed from test work, and can achieve the target plant throughput 
and grind size (P80 of 75 µm). 
It has been demonstrated that the Nyanzaga and Kilimani deposits are ‘free-milling’ and amenable to gold 
recovery by a standard gravity and CIL flowsheet.  Gravity/cyanidation variability test work at optimised 
flowsheet conditions determined that average gold extractions by ore type ranged between 82.3% and 
96.1%. Low to moderate sodium cyanide and lime consumptions have been observed through test work. 
It was noted that the Nyanzaga and Kilimani deposit ores contain elevated concentrations of mercury, arsenic 
and antimony. The process design includes a mercury handling circuit to mitigate the health hazards 
associated with mercury exposure. Test work and  modelling indicates that soluble arsenic and soluble 
antimony will not have a significant effect on potential economic recovery of gold in CIL and that soluble 
arsenic and soluble antimony will be contained within the tailings and process water systems. Provision has 
been made in sustaining capital for a water treatment plant should arsenic or antimony present operational 
challenges in the future. pH control is included in the process control design to mitigate gold passivation that 
can occur at high pH due to elevated antimony levels. 
25.5 RECOVERY METHODS 
The process plant has been designed and costed to Feasibility Study level, and  is based on a robust 
metallurgical flowsheet designed for optimum recovery with minimal operating costs. The flowsheet is based 
on unit operations that are well proven in industry.  Processing parameters, costs, and revenues are well 
understood and can be considered reliable predictors of the mineral processing performance at Nyanzaga. 
Perseus intends to proceed with detailed design of the mineral processing plant.

25.6 PROJECT INFRASTRUCTURE 
Infrastructure for the process plant, and the Project more widely, has been considered and defined to 
Feasibility Study level. Key enabling infrastructure for the Project includes the Ngoma bypass road, 220 kV 
connection to the TANESCO grid, external co mmunications, water abstraction system from Lake Victoria, 
TSF, MSA, permanent accommodation camp, and other operational buildings. 
Perseus intends to proceed with detailed design of Project enabling infrastructure. 
25.7 ENVIRONMENT, SOCIAL IMPACT AND PERMITTING 
The Environmental and Social Management Plan is being updated for resubmission to the NEMC. This will 
allow for construction of the Project in line with the design concept variations made since the previous plan 
submission. A mine closure plan with associated costs will need to be developed within one year of 
commencing operations. 
A permitting pathway has been generated that encompasses all other necessary permits and approvals and 
Perseus has commenced engagement with various Ministries and authorities to progress the permitting 
process. 
A RAP housing construction program is underway, and the scheduling of house builds will be sequenced to 
ensure that areas of the SML are available to achieve Project development scope and schedule. 
Although a number of environmental and social impacts have been identified, it is expected that these will 
be successfully abated through implementation of a range of mitigations and management measures. At the 
same time there will be many positive impacts  expected, including improved housing, community 
infrastructure, community contributions to improve services, livelihood developments and employment 
opportunities for local community members. 
25.8 ECONOMIC ANALYSIS 
Economic Analysis of the Nyanzaga Gold Project has shown that at an assumed gold price of $2,100/oz, the 
project is economically viable and the Mineral Reserves, stated in Section 15, are therefore supported. The 
Project pre-tax NPV10% (pre-tax) is most sensitive to variations in gold price.

26.1 MINERAL RESOURCES 
Perseus is currently conducting planned drilling programs within the Nyanzaga area, which aim to add to 
reported Mineral Resources. The work program will involve additional drilling as both infill and at depth for 
each of Nyanzaga and Kilimani. The works are estimated to be approximately $11.8M. Approximately $5.1M 
of this cost is contingent on results of the initial works. 
26.2 MINERAL RESERVES 
Once the additional drilling referred to in Section 26.1, the additional geotechnical drilling and test work 
referred to in Section 26.3, and the additional metallurgical test work referred to in Section 26.4 has been 
completed, Mineral Reserves should be updated based on any additions to Mineral Resource s and any 
changes to geotechnical and ore processing parameters, and the results of such work should be publicly 
released. This work will be completed in-house by Perseus and will not incur additional cost. 
26.3 MINING METHODS 
The contractor mining tender process for the Nyanzaga Gold Project should continue in order to test the 
market for real-world mining costs and enable mobilisation of a suitable open pit mining contractor in time 
for the pre-strip of the Nyanzaga Gold Project. Costs for this work is estimated to be $120,000.  
Perseus intends to complete additional geotechnical drilling, test work and analysis to improve confidence 
and precision of pit and waste dump geotechnical parameters. Costs are estimated at $3.5M for drilling and 
$370,000 for test work and analysis. 
Perseus has also commenced a program to  increase knowledge relating to the potential for aci d rock 
drainage (ARD) generation from waste rock material. This will consider distribution of potentially acid 
forming (PAF) materials and develop detailed plans for waste d ump design that includes encapsulation. 
Estimated cost for this work is $175,000.   
26.4 MINERAL PROCESSING AND METALLURGICAL TESTING 
Perseus intends to complete the following metallurgical test work and analysis  to further  improve 
understanding of ore variability and improve confidence and precision of operating and cost parameters used 
for ongoing business planning processes: 
• Additional comminution and gravity/leach variability test work from recent and current drilling programs 
conducted on the Nyanzaga and Kilimani deposits. 
• Additional optimisation test work for pre-oxidation and CIL oxygenation. 
• Additional test work to optimise operational parameters for the cyanide detoxification process. 
• Test work to support the design of a water treatment plant to treat any excess water to discharge quality, 
should this requirement be confirmed during ongoing technical studies. 
• Review sample characterisation by ore type in line with evolving geological interpretation of the 
Nyanzaga and Kilimani deposits, as additional drilling information becomes available. 
• Update ore specific operating and cost parameters, based on the review of sample characterisation and 
the body of proposed additional metallurgical test work noted above.

• Ongoing testing of the proposed raw water source, to understand the impact that a wider range of

Completion of this additional test work is estimated to cost $600,000.   
Perseus also recommends that metallurgical test work programs  are conducted on future ore sources

Project process plant. The cost of future ore test work programs is dependent on the occurrence, size and 
nature of future ore deposits, but costs for these programs typically fall in the range of $100,000 to $300,000 
and funding is requested as part of the annual budget cycles. 
26.5 RECOVERY METHODS 
It is recommended to proceed with detailed design of the mineral processing plant. Detailed design forms 
part of the proposed EPCM scope , and the EPCM scope has been fully costed in the Project capital cost 
estimate presented in Section 21.1. 
$35.4M has been included in the capital cost estimate for Perth-office based  EPCM (e ngineering, 
procurement and construction management) services for the process plant, as well as infrastructure items 
(Section 26.6) within the EPCM contractor’s scope. Note that detailed design is only one component of the 
EPCM services. 
26.6 PROJECT INFRASTRUCTURE 
It is recommended to proceed with detailed design of Project enabling infrastructure. Detailed design forms 
part of the proposed EPCM scope, and the EPCM scope has been fully costed in the Project capital cost 
estimate presented in Section 21.1. 
The following costs have been included in the capital cost estimate for the full range of EPCM (engineering, 
procurement and construction management) services: 
• $35.4M for the process plant and infrastructure items within the EPCM contractor’s Perth-office based 
scope. 
• $2.3M for the TSF, water abstraction and surface water management scopes. 
• $1.4M for the grid power supply scope. 
• $0.1M for specialist building architecture assistance. 
 
Note that detailed design is only one component of the EPCM services listed above. 
Perseus will also proceed with a study considering a full -capacity power station located adjacent to the 
Project 220 kV switchyard. This study will evaluate meeting the process plant's peak demand through the 
deployment of high-speed generators connected to the 11 kV switchboard on-site. The concept will consider 
operation in parallel with the grid supply, accommodating both reduced load conditions and total outages. 
Renewable generation options will also be considered. A cost provision of $150,000 is included within the 
approved corporate Projects budget to progress this study. 
26.7 ENVIRONMENT, SOCIAL IMPACT AND PERMITTING 
Applications for Permits required for the Project, as outlined in Table 4-4, should be made in a timely manner 
in order to support the development and execution of the Nyanzaga Gold Project.  This work will be 
completed in-house by existing Perseus personnel and will not incur additional cost.
